n01-open

Every model has its own instincts. Some go lean, some go thorough, some think about security first. <break time='200ms'/> So which one should design your architecture? <break time='150ms'/> Don't guess. Ask them all.
n02-title
In this episode: comparing AI models side by side, on the same brief and on the same design.
n03-compare
Open Compare. One brief goes to several models at once, and the answers come back side by side.
n04-models
Pick from fourteen models across providers. Here: GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Mistral Large 3, and Kimi K2.6.
n05-run
Same clinic booking brief for all four. <break time='100ms'/> Run.
n06-results
Each result shows its services, connections, groups and workflow steps, with time and tokens. The fastest, the cheapest, and the most thorough are flagged for you.
n07-critique
But numbers aren't judgment. Ask a critic model to rank the designs, and explain why.
n08-present
Or let an AI presenter walk the room through it.
n09-use
Like the winner? One click puts it on the canvas.
n10-yours
And from there, it's your diagram. Move things around until it tells your story.
n11-validate
Now flip it around: one design, reviewed by several models. The same four, each working independently.
n12-vresults
Each model scores the five pillars its own way. They don't always agree, <break time='100ms'/> and that's the point.
n13-consensus
Consensus findings merge them all. Confidence is the share of models that flagged the same issue on their own. <break time='120ms'/> Four out of four? Fix that one first.
n14-usevalidation
Keep the review you trust most, and take it back to the canvas.
n15-close
Four models. One brief. One design. <break time='150ms'/> See where they agree, and decide with evidence.
